text:
Marathon Petroleum has climbed 9.6% over two weeks, with today's modest gain of 0.7% continuing a steady upward trend since mid-September. The driver is escalating Middle East instability—Iran has closed the Strait of Hormuz, Houthi attacks on Saudi infrastructure have intensified, and fresh attacks near Riyadh's airport were reported this week. These supply disruptions push global oil prices sharply higher (Brent crude at $130.80/barrel versus WTI at $107), which benefits refiners like Marathon by widening the margin between what they pay for crude and what they earn selling refined products like gasoline and diesel.

The backdrop amplifies this effect: U.S. refineries are running at 96.8% capacity, meaning they're near peak output and well-positioned to capitalize on higher product prices. With geopolitical tensions looking entrenched rather than fleeting, the market is pricing in sustained strength for refining margins, which is why the stock has momentum rather than a one-day pop.
